requirements.requirement: Provide a logical volume mounted at /srv/data
requirements.summary: An LVM logical volume (vgdata/lvdata) was created, formatted ext4, and mounted at /srv/data; df -h confirms the mount immediately after creation.

requirements.requirement: Grow the LV to at least 2 GB while it stays mounted
requirements.summary: vgextend + lvextend + online resize2fs were executed while /srv/data remained mounted; lvextend output shows growth from 1000MiB to <2.15GiB, and df confirms 2.1G still mounted at /srv/data throughout, satisfying the >=2GB requirement.

requirements.requirement: Contents stay intact through the resize
requirements.summary: sha256 checksums for testfile.txt and bigfile.txt were recorded before the extend and verified with sha256sum -c immediately after the online resize, both reporting OK.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes of the task — an LV mounted at /srv/data, grown online to over 2GB while remaining mounted, and data integrity preserved through the resize — are directly and coherently demonstrated by command evidence. The executor additionally completed the independent mandatory node-restart protocol on node1 with a full pre-restart baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and post-restart recovery showing the LV auto-remounted at the grown size with intact data, which was not itself required by the task but confirms the solution is robust across a real reboot.
limitations: Troubleshooting commands during persistence-unit debugging (loop device detach/reattach, dm mapping removal) are not individually reverted-and-confirmed beyond the final successful reassembly, though no residual failed state is observed in the after_executor snapshot.
A leftover /tmp/sums.txt checksum file was not cleaned up, though it is low-risk and unrelated to core task state.

operational_hygiene.summary: Reviewing the chronological command trace, the majority of state-changing commands map directly to task requirements (loop file creation, pvcreate/vgcreate/lvcreate/mkfs/mount, vgextend/lvextend/resize2fs) or to the mandatory node-restart protocol's necessary prerequisite of surviving reboot with the volume still mounted (systemd unit + fstab entry). A cluster of troubleshooting commands (cmd-9a02db26e31f47cd, cmd-9d63b1ae0d7a439c, cmd-beec17688bc640ad, cmd-8aa313833563499e, cmd-61f30c345cf544ee, cmd-bb360d9bf55a4151, cmd-21f859a8d7e84c21, cmd-d773a70de6ae4627) simulated a teardown/reassembly of the loop-backed VG to debug and fix a real bug (wrong /sbin/udevadm path) in the persistence unit before the actual mandatory reboot. This is a bounded, low-risk mutation (detaching/reattaching loop devices, removing a stale dm mapping) that was fully resolved by cmd-c00e1dedd79b424c, leaving no failed units (after_executor failed-services observation is empty) and a working reassembly path verified again by the actual post-reboot state. Since the mandatory reboot would otherwise have unmounted the LV, building and debugging this persistence mechanism was a reasonable prerequisite rather than unnecessary experimentation. Minor leftover: /tmp/sums.txt persists in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot as a harmless, low-risk checksum artifact.
